proposals.title: Trap-true twins, and one Twin control on every question
proposals.what:
The problem, measured on the bank: a fresh seed of the same template leaves out the misconception the student picked 40.8% of the time. That is 10,802 of 26,469 trap and seed pairs, over 12 seeds per template, in 273 of the 386 templates. It is still 39.6% when letters and units are folded together, because each item draws only 3 of its template's mistakes. So the spec's repair ('the same template on a fresh seed', §3.3.4) and its rule that 'two clean answers on the template close the mistake' often never offer the trap again.

The fix:
(1) drill._fresh takes `trap: norm`. It walks seeds from a start derived from (learner, template, n), skips seeds already in attempts(learner, template, seed), and takes the first item whose reasons, or spr_mistakes, normalise to that norm. Measured: 98.4% of traps come back within 60 seeds, with a median walk of 1 seed and a 90th percentile of 7, at 0.26 ms a seed. If nothing is found, it serves the plain twin with the line 'This type didn't offer that trap again; here is the closest.'
(2) progress.record stores the norms each attempt offered. A trap's owed count drops only on clean answers to items that offered its norm. Other clean answers still count for mastery.
(3) Every repair, redo, check-in (R9), Spot the trap, Try one like this and QOTD 'like' drill passes `trap` whenever a trap exists.
(4) One verb, 'Twin', replaces 'Another one like this', 'Try one like this', 'Fresh one like this', '5 more like this', 'Another like this' and 'New one like this'. It has one glyph (two offset squares) and key T, which is free in §2.8's runner map. T works after answering in the runner and anywhere in the player.
(5) `UI.twin(anchor, ctx)` opens a menu:
   - Twin: the same trap if you missed, else the same type.
   - Easier / Harder: the same template when it has that tier (59 do), else the same skill at that tier, and labelled so.
   - Same trap in other types (n): a want-regex walk across templates that share the norm; 79 norms recur.
   - Twin x5: an inline set.
   - Print 10: a worksheet with a key.
(6) A twin's header reads 'Twin · watch for: used the diameter as the radius'. The pref twin_tell (default on) controls it; turning it off gives honest self-testing.
(7) Sittings, sets, worksheets and contests say 'Twin test' / 'Twin this set' with the same glyph.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's QOTD 'More practice' and QBank retries either re-show the same item, with unlimited retries, or open a generic list. A fixed bank cannot make a new question that contains the exact trap you fell for. This also makes our own core promise true: today it holds only about 59% of the time.
proposals.needs: F5: extend _fresh's want walk from 12 to 60 seeds, match spr_mistakes too, and add the `trap` field to the §2.6 drill body. F4: store offered norms on attempts and change the closing rule in R9 and progress.record. F3: UI.twin and the T key in the runner and player maps. Every question surface swaps its own button for UI.twin: S3 QOTD and Try one now, S4 verdict, S6 player, S8 contest review, S9 word examples, S10 pane.

proposals.title: Points on the table: one score-gain forecast that ranks everything
proposals.what:
A new `server/points.py`.

Model:
(1) For each skill and each type the learner has met, p is the chance of a clean first-try right answer, by tier. It comes from the learner's clean attempts (R8 rules: no repeat, disputed or void rows; a guess counts half), shrunk toward the field's first-try rate on that template and tier (k = 8). Once Compete fills item_ratings and learner ratings, p = logistic(rating minus item rating).
(2) The expected Math section walks blueprint.slots() for module 1 and for both module 2s. It sums WEIGHT x p per slot (a domain's skills in proportion to blueprint.by_domain), routes with ROUTE_UP_AT, caps with LOWER_ROUTE_CEILING and scales with scoring._interpolate. These are the same functions that mark a real sitting.
(3) A skill's gain is the expected score with that skill's p raised to 0.85 (STRONG), minus the score now. The low and high ends come from evidence n.
(4) Minutes to that gain = questions to reach Strong (from the learner's own rate of mastery per answer, 12 per +0.1 by default) x the learner's median seconds on that skill.
(5) A route line appears when expected module-1 right answers are within 1.5 questions of 14/22: 'About 1 question short of the harder module 2. The lower route caps you at 580.'

Why it matters: under the blueprint, one Advanced Math skill carries about 11.7% of the section's points and one PSDA skill about 2.1%. That is a 5x difference no student knows by feel.

API: `GET /api/points` returns {now:{low,high}, route:{short_by, gain}, skills:[{topic, gain:[lo,hi], minutes, per_hour, why}], traps:[{id, gain}], types:[top 20]}. It is cached per learner until the next answer.

Where it shows (one hook per owner):
* Today, Up next: the reason line gains '≈ +12 points · 18 min', and progress.coach adds a points-per-minute term to its score.
* Results: a 'Points on the table' card with 19 range bars sorted by gain, minutes and a Practise button on each row, a sort of Points | Per hour, and a total ('about +60 available from 560–700').
* Plan: step 4's 'Use suggestions' picks the top skills by points per hour. The SplitBar labels what each share buys, and the plan's trajectory is now + the gains bought by the planned minutes.
* Review: Redo sorts by 'Most points' by default, with '≈ +3' on each row.
* Report: the what-if line uses this model.
* Palette, Suggested: 'Biggest win: Nonlinear functions · +18'.

Copy always says 'about' and shows a range, and links to a Help anchor, 'How points are estimated', which carries scoring.py's own statement that the scale is a heuristic.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's plan Progress tab offers 'Accuracy by domain, weakest first' and an aiReason, and its dashboard shows no score until a full four-module test. Nothing there turns a weakness into points and minutes, weighs a skill by its share of the test, or knows about the routing cliff. Pricing each skill needs clean evidence per type, which only fresh, never-repeated items give.
proposals.needs: F4: clean-attempt rules and estimate.py. The blueprint module's slots and by_domain functions (blueprint.py, owned by S5). scoring._interpolate. Field first-try rates per template and tier (S4's per-type stats). item_ratings (S8), optional. Consumers: S3, S6, S7, S10, S1 (Me), F2 (palette). Add a §2.9 contract line: F4 or a new owner provides points.forecast(learner).

proposals.title: Autopilot: 'Study 30 min', one interleaved session that runs the whole day
proposals.what:
Where it launches:
* A primary pill on Today's hero, 'Study 30 min', with chips 10 · 20 · 30 · 45 · 60. The default is today's plan minutes left, else the daily goal, else 20.
* The same launcher in the sidebar Today card, the Q sheet and the palette ('study 20'), plus a manifest shortcut.

How it picks: `POST /api/drill {pool:'auto', minutes:N}` makes one practice sitting whose next_question picks each item when it is asked, in this order:
(1) Check-ins due (pool checks).
(2) Open traps ranked by points, as trap-true twins.
(3) The plan's focus topics, else the points engine's top skills, at the adaptive tier (R33).
(4) One keep-warm item (pool review) every 8th question.

Interleaving rules:
* Never the same template twice in a row.
* At most 3 of one skill in a row.
* The repair after a miss comes 1 to 3 questions later, not at once, so it is spaced.

In the runner: the top bar shows a goal ring ('18 of 30 min') and a chip naming the segment and why ('Check-in · fixed Sep 12', 'Fixing · sign of the slope', 'Focus · Circles'). There is no per-question countdown.

End: at N minutes the set ends at the next question boundary with a summary. It shows minutes, answered, mistakes closed, check-ins passed, the skills that moved (before → after bars) and '≈ +4 points banked' (the points delta), with 'Keep going · 10 min' and 'Done'.

Plan and history: every answer is tagged with the plan task it serves (fix, recheck or focus, by topic), so Today's list ticks itself and the day is done by the minutes rule. Pause and Save & exit work as in any set. History lists it as 'Autopilot · 30 min'.

Words: when words are due and prefs.words_goal > 0, a 3-card word interstitial comes every 10 minutes (workspace quiz mode). It can be skipped.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no single 'just study' action. Plan tasks launch one at a time and are ticked by hand, a QBank session never ends, and nothing mixes repairs, reviews and new work. A finite bank cannot run an open-ended interleaved session without repeating itself.
proposals.needs: F5: pool 'auto' in the §2.6 body with per-step picking. Points engine, with progress.coach as the fallback. S7: task tagging and the done rules for fix and recheck by the templates served. S3: hero launcher. F2: sidebar card, palette parsing, manifest shortcut. F3: a runner top-bar slot for the goal ring and segment chip. S9: optional interstitial via the words quiz.

proposals.title: Solve it with Desmos: a verified graphing route pre-loaded per question
proposals.what:
Bank side (T-bank):
* Add `Item.desmos: list[str]` (Desmos LaTeX) and `Item.desmos_read` (what to read off: 'x where the graphs cross', 'the y-intercept', 'the positive zero', 'the value of k on the slider') for templates with a graphing route.
* Coverage from a stem scan: about 130 of 386 templates carry an equation, mostly nonlinear equations (24/32), nonlinear functions (24/36), linear functions (14/23), systems (12/20) and linear in one variable (11/18).
* Build check: the audit solves the route numerically in Python from the same expressions (bisection on the difference, or by evaluation) and requires it to land on the key. A route that fails does not ship.
* `tools/desmos_coverage.py` prints 'n of 386 types have a verified Desmos route'. Like spr_mistakes, it ships partial and grows.

UI:
* After answering, in review, on the type page and in the playbook, a 'Desmos' action opens UI.calc (docked or floating) through setExpressions. The point to read is labelled, with one line: 'Graph both sides; they cross at x = 7.'
* In practice before answering, 'Show the Desmos route' is a hint that files the answer as assisted: it counts half, like I'm guessing, and does not close a trap.
* Never offered in a live test, contest or unanswered challenge. It is available in their review.

Stats:
* qstate records calc_used per question.
* Per type: 'By hand: 2:10 average, 64% right · With Desmos: 0:45, 92%'.
* The playbook and the type page list 'Use Desmos on these 9 types' where the route is verified and the student's hand time is over 60 s.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep embeds Desmos as an empty panel and never shows how to use it on the question in front of you, although Desmos methods are the most sought-after SAT Math tactic. No finite bank has a checked graphing route for every item. Ours is computed and verified from each item's own numbers.
proposals.needs: T-bank: the Item fields, per-template expressions and the audit check. F3: UI.calc.setExpressions and a verdict-actions slot. F4: calc_used in qstate. Surfaces: S4, S6, S10, the type pages and the playbook. A Desmos production key (open question 15).

proposals.title: The 386-type map and a page for every question type
proposals.what:
Map, `/types/`:
* 19 skill rows under 4 domains, one 14px cell per type.
* Cell states: Not met (dashed), Met (outline), Open mistake (ink with an orange dot), Fixed (ink ✓), Proven (orange fill), Check-in due (orange ring).
* A legend with counts ('Proven 112 · Met 57 · Open 9 · Not met 208').
* Filters: skill, state, format, tier, Desmos route.
* Header: '112 of 386 types proven · 71% of the test's weight' (weighted by the blueprint).
* Actions:
   - Prove 10: a custom test under test rules, one fresh question per unproven type, highest weight first.
   - Meet 10 new types (pool untried).
   - Print the map.
* Proven means: the last 2 clean first-try answers on unseen seeds are right, the latest within 30 days, and no trap is open. It is lost on a missed check-in or any clean miss.

Type page, `/types/?t=circles.arc` (public):
* A student-facing title and a one-line 'what it asks'. T-bank writes these for the 386 templates, because skill labels repeat, e.g. 'linear equation'.
* Skill, formats and tiers, plus weight ('about 1 question in 30 on SAT Math').
* Worked example: from the reserved seeds (900000+), with the key, the rationale and every option's trap; 'Another example' shows the next seed.
* Learn it: 2 worked examples, then 3 of your own, inline.
* The traps: every reason this type produces (from /api/types), each with the field's share of misses, your count, and 'Spot it'.
* Your history (UI.history), and your time against the field median and 95 s.
* The Desmos route, when one exists.
* Official match: the College Board items this type was learned from (sources.py; references only).
* Actions: Twin x5, Practise timed, Print 20 with key, Log a mistake of this type, Copy link.

Wiring: every question anywhere gets 'About this type' in Details (session popover, report player, review pane, QOTD, word examples). In the palette, a Question types row runs a drill on Enter and opens the page on Shift+Enter.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep stops at 29 skills, has no lessons, and has no view of which kinds of problem you have covered. A map of every type with a live teaching page for each only works when the bank is organised as types that never run out of examples.
proposals.needs: T-bank: titles and one-liners for 386 templates. F5: /api/types, /api/types/{t}/example, and a custom test by templates. F4: attempts and traps. S4: field per-type stats. F2: palette. F3: UI.history. S1: link from Me and the progress view. S7: may target unproven types. A sources index built from satbank/topics/*/sources.py.

proposals.title: Paste any question, get its type: from Bluebook or a textbook straight to unlimited twins
proposals.what:
Where: a 'Paste a question' textarea in the palette, and as the first step of the quick sheet's Log a mistake tab.

Server: `POST /api/match {text ≤ 2000}` returns the top 3 templates, each with a score and a generated example (reserved seeds).

Index: TF-IDF over words and bigrams with numbers stripped, built at startup from 8 example stems per template plus the titles. It is in memory and uses only the standard library. Measured on held-out seeds of our own stems: the right type is first 94% of the time and in the top 3 98% of the time (382 types). The right skill is first 98% of the time.

UI:
* Three cards, 'Is it like this?', each showing its example.
* Picking one offers: Twin x5 (drill templates), Learn this type (type page), and Log it as a mistake (the type preselected, then its misconception list, with the pasted text kept as the trap's note, up to 1000 characters).
* Below a score threshold, it falls back to today's pick-the-skill flow.
* Text that reads as R&W gets 'We only have Math so far' and a link to Words' In-context quiz.

Nothing is stored unless the student logs it.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no search at all. Even with search, a fixed bank can only return a similar item. Ours takes a question from anywhere, whether a Bluebook test, class or a book, and turns it into unlimited fresh twins and a tracked mistake in two taps. Today's Log a mistake needs a skill, a type and an example check.
proposals.needs: F5: /api/types and drill templates, plus a new /api/match (in api_bank.py). F2: palette group and quick-sheet step. S10: note on logged traps. Type pages, optional.

proposals.title: Habit profile: the few mistakes behind all your mistakes
proposals.what:
The habit list: a fixed list of 14 habit classes, each normalised misconception tagged with one:
* answered the wrong quantity (the other solution, an intermediate value, a given value)
* sign slip
* operation swap
* part vs whole
* inverted ratio / wrong base
* squares and roots
* distribution / order of operations
* formula mix (radius/diameter, area/perimeter, sine/tangent)
* units and conversion
* misread graph or table
* slope vs intercept
* statistics mix-up
* probability denominator
* arithmetic slip

Tagging: `satbank/habits.py` holds an ordered regex list plus per-template overrides. A first regex pass already tags 52% of the 2,125 distinct normalised reasons; the goal is 95% with overrides, the rest 'other'. A coverage script prints the share. Each habit also gets one authored 'tell', 14 lines written once (e.g. 'Before solving, underline what the last sentence asks for').

Screens:
* A Habits card on Results and Me, ranked: 'Answered the wrong quantity · 31% of your misses · 9 types in 5 skills', with a 12-week sparkline and the field's rate.
* Per habit:
   - Habit drill · 10: a want-regex drill across every template whose reasons carry that habit, mixed skills, trap-true.
   - Spot it · 8: Spot the trap on that habit.
   - Trap maker: 'Type what a student who adds instead of multiplies would get', a grid-in checked against the Mis value.
* The report groups a sitting's misses by habit.
* Review filters by habit.

Cue (pref habit_cues, on): in practice, on a type that carries your top habit, a one-line tell shows above the options before any selection, so it can never depend on your choice or leak the key. It fades after 3 clean answers on that type, and is never shown in tests or contests.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's 'Distractor Analysis' is prose per item. Its distractors carry no labels, so it can never see that half of a student's misses in five different skills are one habit. Only a bank with a named misconception behind every wrong option can add them up across topics and then drill that habit on fresh questions.
proposals.needs: T-bank or F4: a habit tag on each norm (relates to open question 18, Mis.tag). F5: want across templates. S6: Results card and report grouping. S1: Me. S4: the cue in the session. S10: Spot and the habit filter.

proposals.title: First visit: 'Find your next 50 points' in 12 questions, no account, no gate
proposals.what:
New learner: for a learner with no attempts, Today's hero becomes one card: 'Find where your points are · 12 questions · about 12 min · no sign-up'.

The placement:
* 12 fresh questions weighted by the blueprint: Algebra 4, Advanced Math 4, PSDA 2, Geometry & Trig 2.
* The tier steps up or down per R33, untimed, with a visible pace chip.
* It is a normal drill (source 'start'), so it files mastery and mistakes.

The result, shown straight away:
* A wide, honest band: 'about 480–640 from 12 questions, a module tightens it'.
* The top 3 skills by points on the table, with minutes each.
* The named traps it caught.
* Actions: 'Start with Nonlinear functions · 10' (primary), 'Build my plan' (prefilled from this), 'Take a module for a tighter band'.
* 'Save to your email' comes after, as a banner, never before.

The diagnostic stays for a fuller reading.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep puts a Google sign-in wall in front of everything, and shows no score until a full four-module test. A student switching over gets a band, their three biggest point leaks and a first set in about 12 minutes, without making an account.
proposals.needs: F5: source 'start' with the adaptive rule. Points engine. S3: new-student state. S7: plan prefill from the result. A decision on R38 / open question 8 (the diagnostic's own gate).

proposals.title: Your SAT playbook and a real final week
proposals.what:
`/playbook/` is built live from the student's data and prints on one A4 or Letter page. It has six parts:
(1) Your 8 costliest traps, ranked by points. Each has its habit tell and one worked twin: key, the wrong option and why.
(2) Pace plan: your median per domain against 95 s. 'First pass: flag and skip these types; they take you 2:40+ and you get under 50%' lists the slowest, lowest-yield types, weighted by the blueprint. 'Bank these: fast and right'.
(3) Desmos list: verified-route types where your hand time is over 60 s.
(4) Grid-in rules you have broken: 5/6-character entries, fraction forms, taken from S5's validator rejections and wrong SPR entries.
(5) The math words you looked up.
(6) The test-day checklist.

Final-week mode starts when exam_date is 7 days away or less. Today leads with 'Final week':
* every fixed mistake is brought forward as a check-in sweep, spread over the days;
* one full section at the real test's start time on a matching day (the doors-close time from the countdown);
* no new types;
* the playbook on the eve, which stays a rest day.

The plan's Final phase uses the same rules.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's last week looks like any other week, with a countdown. A one-page personal trap sheet with a worked twin per trap, a skip list from your own timings and a Desmos list needs named mistakes, time per type and generated twins, none of which a fixed bank has.
proposals.needs: S10: traps. S6 or F4: per-type time from attempts.ms. The Desmos proposal, optional. S5: grid-in rejection counts. S9: looked-up words. S3: countdown and checklist. S7: Final phase hooks. Print CSS (F1).

proposals.title: Offline pack for the phone
proposals.what:
This reverses §2.14's 'no service worker'.

Where: 'Download 30 for offline' in Practice and the quick sheet, plus auto-refresh on the installed app when pref offline_pack is on.

The pack:
* The server issues a normal practice drill whose 30 items (the coach's pick, check-ins due, trap twins) come in one response with keys, rationales and reasons.
* Practice only. Never tests, contests, QOTD or challenge items; deps.access decides.
* Each trap-bearing item carries one trap-true twin, so a miss still gets its repair offline.

Caching: a small `web/sw.js` caches the session page, question.js, runner.js, ui.css, the fonts and the pack. Figures are inline SVG, so they work offline. The calculator button reads 'Needs a connection'.

Answers:
* They go through UI.saveQueue's localStorage mirror with their ms and client time.
* On reconnect they flush in order.
* The server accepts them for untimed practice.
* A banner reads 'Offline · 12 of 30 answered · syncs when you are back'.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep needs a connection for every screen. A commute becomes study time, and each pack is new questions, which a finite bank could not keep supplying without burning through itself.
proposals.needs: F5: prefetch pack (drill create returning all items). F3: saveQueue with late-accept semantics. F0/F2: sw.js registration and the manifest. S4: the session page's offline mode. F4: late answers accepted for untimed practice.

proposals.title: Paper versions for classes and tutors: every student a different test, one class report
proposals.what:
Where: 'Print N versions' (2 to 60) on any set, assignment or worksheet.

The versions: each is the same template in every slot with its own seeds (twins). Each page carries a version code (e.g. K7Q-12), a numbered answer grid and a QR code. The key booklet is by version, and each wrong option has its misconception.

Answer entry, at `/s/?c=CODE&v=K7Q-12`: the student, or the teacher for them, types answers into a 22-field grid in about a minute. Nothing else is needed.

Results: they feed the same owner results and class misconception report as online sets, e.g. '9 of 24 used the base angle as the central angle'. The report works even though every student had different numbers, because wrong answers map to named misconceptions. 'Assign a repair to these 9' follows.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's teacher tools are hidden, assign one fixed set that students can copy, and have no paper route. A fixed bank cannot print 30 different but equal tests with keys on demand.
proposals.needs: S2: classes and assignments. F6: sets (kind 'paper' with a versions JSON). The S10/S4 worksheet print. F5: exact items via deps.access.

proposals.title: Figures and math a screen reader can use
proposals.what:
T-bank adds `Item.figure_alt`, generated from the item's params by each topic's figure builder, e.g. 'Circle with center O. Points A, G and P lie on the circle. Arc AGP is marked 108 degrees.' A build check requires every labelled point and every given measure in params to appear in the description.

Tables get real `<th>` headers and a caption.

Stems and options get spoken-math aria labels ('15 pi over 4', 'x squared minus 5').

A 'Read aloud' action (speechSynthesis, as Words' UI.speak) reads the stem and options. It is off in live tests unless the extended-time accommodation is set.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's figures are images with no text alternative, and they float beside the text. Because we draw every figure from known numbers, each one can say exactly what it shows. That serves students with low vision and anyone studying by ear.
proposals.needs: T-bank: figure builders in satbank/topics/*/figures.py and render.py, plus the audit check. F3: workspace aria and Read aloud. S9: UI.speak. S5: the accommodation pref.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A date eyebrow, 'Good morning, {name}', and four status chips (streak, minutes today, SAT in N days, plan progress), each linking to its card.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their hero is the same date eyebrow and greeting. The chips repeat figures the cards below already show, and the hero starts nothing.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Make the hero the day's launcher: the Autopilot pill 'Study 30 min' with minute chips, plus one computed line, 'About +38 points on the table · 3 check-ins due · SAT in 45 days', from the points engine. The greeting moves into the eyebrow. Up next stays for the single next item.

parity_gaps.spec_says: One rationale per item, and every option's named misconception under it after the reveal.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their review shows 'Justification:' then 'Distractor Analysis:' with one line per wrong option. That is the same shape: one explanation plus a line per distractor.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Four steps: Where you are, Where you're going, Time you have, What to focus on. Score sliders, date chips, minutes chips, weekday tiles, Focus/Normal/Strong per domain with a cap, then Create. Better defaults and a pace tag than theirs.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Step titles, order and controls match theirs one for one. A student with 300 answers still walks four screens to be told what the data already knows.

parity_gaps.feature: 'Why this?' on tasks and served questions
parity_gaps.spec_says: Fact lines: open mistakes by name, accuracy, days since the skill was worked, focus share, timing gap.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their 'Why this task?' expanding aiReason is the same slot. Ours has truer text, but it is still a justification after the fact.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Every Why carries its price and its consequence, e.g. '≈ +6 points · 14 min · closes 2 of 3 open mistakes; skipping moves the Circles check-in to Fri'. Add a one-tap Swap to the next-best task by points per minute.

parity_gaps.spec_says: R16: latest, range, mean3, combined band, confidence {level, reason}, trend (±20 = steady), routed_up.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their summary API returns the same structure: per-section average/min/max, confidence {level, label, reason}, trend {direction, delta} and a headline.

parity_gaps.spec_says: R16: a sitting ranked among each learner's first standard sitting of the same kind, shown only when n ≥ 20.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: This is their rule ('N% scored at or below you on their first attempt', ranked sittings only). On a new site it stays hidden for months.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add standing per type, which fills in quickly because every first-try answer on a type counts: 'On this type: right more often than 58% of students, faster than 64% (n=212)'. Show it in the verdict, the type page and the report. Keep the sitting percentile for when n allows.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Identity card with 2x4 tiles, ranks snapshot, goals, preferences, skills, score trend, what keeps catching you, achievements, heatmap, recent activity, question types met, saved, account.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their /profile card list, extended. The page is a record, and no card on it is something a student works toward.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Make the 386-type map the centrepiece ('112 of 386 types proven · 71% of the test's weight'), with the Habits card beside it. The progress link, and a shareable image of the map, lead with it.

parity_gaps.spec_says: R17: title, category, details, up to 10 images, a context box with (template, seed), bounded disputes, replies from a person in Settings.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their modal has the same fields. Ours adds replies, but a dispute still waits for a person.
parity_gaps.upgrade: On 'Wrong answer key' or 'More than one right answer', the server regenerates the item, re-runs audit and verify plus the template's official-source check, and replies in the modal within a second. Example: 'Re-checked: 75/360 x 18π = 15π/4. Option B is what 180° for a full turn gives.' Then 'Still wrong? Send to a person', which keeps the bounded dispute. A failed re-check flags the template for every future seed. Screenshots become optional for question reports.

parity_gaps.spec_says: An email 6-digit code (needs SMTP), a pairing code with QR and approval, or the device code. Anonymous-first.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Anonymous-first beats their wall on day one. But their Google sign-in is one tap on any new device, and ours is slower there, or impossible without SMTP.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add 'Continue with Google'. Verify the ID token through Google's tokeninfo endpoint with urllib, so no new dependency, and map it onto users.learner. Keep anonymous-first. Put 'Continue on your phone' (the pairing QR) in the account menu on every page.

parity_gaps.spec_says: R38 keeps the name-and-email step before the diagnostic's result (open question 8).
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their auth wall, moved to the moment a new student cares most.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Result first, save after. Make the no-account 12-question 'Find your points' start the new-student path, with 'Save to your email' offered afterwards as a banner.

parity_gaps.spec_says: None. Open question 17 leaves official replicas out.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Below parity. Their Question Bank toggle serves 1,921 official College Board Math items, a main reason students use them.
parity_gaps.upgrade: On every type page and in each question's Details, list the official College Board items the type was learned from, by set and item. satbank's sources.py reproduces 1,030 official items from their parameters, and the audit matches the College Board's own answers. Link to the College Board's free source and copy no content. Add a 'Checked against N official items' line. Offer unlimited twins of each: their official pool runs out at 1,921; ours is checked against those items and never runs out.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A Math bank only. R&W appears as optional score fields, Words, and custom plan tasks.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Below parity. TopTierPrep covers both sections, so a student preparing for the whole SAT keeps them for R&W.
